answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a terrace as the anchor of the cost. A comet stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a vault...
